statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-109475 (GHSA-3g4v-f5gv-c7xf) is a .NET denial of service: the managed HttpListener can recursively process an unterminated request line and exhaust the process stack. Microsoft fixed it in .NET 10.0.15 and lists the .NET runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, from 10.0.0 through 10.0.14 as affected (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-3g4v-f5gv-c7xf, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/500, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.15/10.0.15.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.24 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries; 10.0.15-r0 is built from the dotnet/dotnet v10.0.115 source tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v10.0.115). Scanned all 154 packages of the seven published builds (10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.12-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside their nupkg and tar.gz archives: every build ships System.Net.HttpListener.dll from its own .NET release, in the shared runtime of dotnet10-runtime and in the SDK and runtime archive held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap; the earlier builds carry 10.0.8 through 10.0.14 and 10.0.15-r0 carries 10.0.15 on both architectures. The range ends at 10.0.15-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-109475 (GHSA-3g4v-f5gv-c7xf) is a .NET denial of service: the managed HttpListener implementation used on Linux and macOS can process an unterminated request line recursively and exhaust the process stack. Microsoft lists the .NET 8.0 runtime, including the linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64 runtime packs, as affected up to 8.0.33 and fixed in 8.0.34 (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-3g4v-f5gv-c7xf, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.34/8.0.34.md); the fix replaces the recursive read callback chain with a ReadNextChunkFragment loop. DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries; its published builds are 8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0. We unpacked every package of 8.0.34-r0 for x86_64 and aarch64 (11 per architecture), including the nupkg and other archives inside them: every implementation copy of System.Net.HttpListener.dll (in dotnet8-runtime, in the .NET SDK and the runtime and ILCompiler packs held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap) reports .NET 8.0.34 and contains ReadNextChunkFragment, while every 8.0.33-r0 implementation copy lacks it; the other copies are reference assemblies (in the targeting packs, the API documentation transport package and the source-build reference packages), which hold API signatures and no implementation code. The earlier builds carry .NET 8.0.23 through 8.0.33. The range ends at 8.0.34-r0, the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-109475 (GHSA-3g4v-f5gv-c7xf) is a .NET denial of service issue: the managed HttpListener can recursively process an unterminated request line and exhaust the process stack. Microsoft lists the .NET 9.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, as affected up to 9.0.22 and fixed in 9.0.23 (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-3g4v-f5gv-c7xf, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/500, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.23/9.0.23.md); between the v9.0.22 and v9.0.23 tags of dotnet/runtime the managed HttpListener's chunked input handling gains a ReadNextChunkFragment method (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/compare/v9.0.22...v9.0.23). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries; 9.0.23-r0 is built from the dotnet/dotnet v9.0.124 source tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v9.0.124), and its assemblies record that tag's commit, f4699d9. In dotnet9-runtime of all eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0 through 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0), for x86_64 and aarch64, the shared runtime's System.Net.HttpListener.dll carries the build's own .NET version; the 9.0.23-r0 copies contain ReadNextChunkFragment and the copies in the earlier builds do not. dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap in each of those builds also holds the .NET shared runtime at the build's own version (9.0.12 through 9.0.22 in the earlier builds, 9.0.23 in 9.0.23-r0). In the 9.0.23-r0 dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap package, read for x86_64, System.Net.HttpListener.dll in the shared runtime, in the extracted .NET runtime pack, in the extracted NativeAOT ILCompiler pack and in the NuGet packages of both packs contains ReadNextChunkFragment; its .NET targeting pack copy, and the copies in the 9.0.23-r0 dotnet9-runtime-artifacts package, are reference assemblies. The range ends at 9.0.23-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-109475 (GHSA-3g4v-f5gv-c7xf) is a .NET denial of service: the managed HttpListener used on Linux and macOS can recursively process an unterminated request line and exhaust the process stack. Microsoft lists the .NET 10.0 runtime packs for linux-x64 and linux-arm64 as affected through 10.0.14 and fixed in 10.0.15, see https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-3g4v-f5gv-c7xf and https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.15/10.0.15.md. The fix, commit https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/commit/5c635731f8588c8bf984494b4be3116670351e68 on the dotnet/dotnet release/10.0.1xx branch and the only change to System.Net.HttpListener between the v10.0.114 and v10.0.115 tags, replaces the recursive read callbacks in the managed HttpListener's request reader and in its ChunkedInputStream with read loops, adding the ReadNextChunkFragment method. DHI dotnet-runtime-10 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's prebuilt .NET Runtime for Linux, checked at build time against the SHA-512 hash Microsoft publishes in https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/releases.json, and each build's version starts with the .NET runtime version it carries. Its published builds are 10.0.9-0, 10.0.10-0, 10.0.11-0, 10.0.12-0, 10.0.13-0, 10.0.14-0, 10.0.15-0 and 10.0.15-1. Unpacked every published dotnet-runtime-10 and dotnet-runtime-10-oci-config package for amd64 and arm64 (checksums verified against the repository index): each dotnet-runtime-10 package holds one shared framework, /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App/<version>, with one System.Net.HttpListener.dll, and the oci-config packages hold one configuration file and its changelog, and no .NET assemblies or native code. In 10.0.9-0 through 10.0.14-0 that assembly reports .NET 10.0.9 through 10.0.14 and lacks ReadNextChunkFragment; in 10.0.15-0 and 10.0.15-1, on both architectures, it reports .NET 10.0.15 and contains ReadNextChunkFragment. Each of those assemblies also records the dotnet/dotnet commit it was built from: 10.0.9-0 through 10.0.14-0 were built from the v10.0.109 through v10.0.114 tags, which do not contain the fix commit, and 10.0.15-0 and 10.0.15-1 from the v10.0.115 tag, which does. The range ends at 10.0.15-0, the first published build with the fix.

Microsoft lists the Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime 10.0 packages up to 10.0.14 as affected and fixed it in .NET 10.0.15 (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-3g4v-f5gv-c7xf, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/500), and the .NET 10.0.15 release notes ship SDK 10.0.404 with the 10.0.15 runtimes (https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.15/10.0.15.md).
